children.title: USPS Clarifies That Machine Postmarks May Postdate Initial Acceptance
children.description_medium: USPS clarified that a machine-applied postmark reflects the first automated processing operation and may therefore show a date later than the day the Postal Service first accepted a mailpiece.  The relevant Domestic Mail Manual language became effective December 24, 2025.  USPS said the clarification reflected longstanding postmarking practice rather than a new change to its postmarking operations.
children.description_long: USPS clarified that a machine-applied postmark reflects the first automated processing operation and may therefore show a date later than the day the Postal Service first accepted a mailpiece. The relevant Domestic Mail Manual language became effective December 24, 2025. USPS said the clarification reflected longstanding postmarking practice rather than a new change to its postmarking operations. This describes the postal standard and USPS’s explanation; it does not establish that the clarification itself caused ballots to arrive late or be rejected. The supplied USPS statement and Postal Bulletin support the operational explanation and effective date. USPS said the postmark clarification described longstanding operations. Separately, EO 14399 set out federal directives concerning citizenship lists and proposed ballot-mail standards. The order’s legal status later changed in litigation in plaintiff states, as described by California’s attorney general; the source does not establish a nationwide disposition. Neither source demonstrates that these separate developments caused a single nationwide delivery crisis. The supplied packet also does not substantiate the exact California late-ballot total or connect late ballots causally to the federal actions. Those matters remain unresolved rather than folded into either event.

children.title: Trump Issues Executive Order on Citizenship Verification and Federal Ballot Mail
children.description_medium: On March 31, 2026, President Donald Trump issued Executive Order 14399, directing the Department of Homeland Security and Social Security Administration to compile state citizenship lists and directing USPS to propose new standards for federal mail ballots.  The order is a separate federal action from USPS’s December 2025 clarification of machine postmarks.
children.description_long: On March 31, 2026, President Donald Trump issued Executive Order 14399, directing the Department of Homeland Security and Social Security Administration to compile state citizenship lists and directing USPS to propose new standards for federal mail ballots. The order is a separate federal action from USPS’s December 2025 clarification of machine postmarks. A California Department of Justice release later described provisions blocked during litigation in plaintiff states. This draft records the order’s directives and notes the later litigation context without claiming a nationwide outcome. The supplied sources do not establish that the order and postmark practices caused a single nationwide ballot-delivery crisis. USPS said the postmark clarification described longstanding operations. Separately, EO 14399 set out federal directives concerning citizenship lists and proposed ballot-mail standards. The order’s legal status later changed in litigation in plaintiff states, as described by California’s attorney general; the source does not establish a nationwide disposition. Neither source demonstrates that these separate developments caused a single nationwide delivery crisis. The supplied packet also does not substantiate the exact California late-ballot total or connect late ballots causally to the federal actions. Those matters remain unresolved rather than folded into either event.
